correctness.rationale: A nonzero real traceless symmetric matrix has both signs, and diagonalization with scaling/sign and interchange of axes gives diag(1,-a,-(1-a)), 0<=a<=1/2. In a frame with last vector n, the n-normal restriction determinant is its last principal cofactor, hence s n_x^2-(1-a)n_y^2-a n_z^2 with s=a(1-a). A nondegenerate indefinite binary form gives four circle zeros and a definite one gives none. The exceptional normals have measure zero also at a=0 (there the determinant is -n_y^2). The nodal set is rectifiable: it is smooth on S^2 for nonsingular A, and two great circles in the singular case. The normalized Crofton factor pi gives 2pi for a great circle intersected twice. The uniform polar coordinate n_x then yields L/(4pi) as the average of sqrt(U/(U+s)) with U=(1-a)cos^2(phi)+a sin^2(phi). At a=0 this equals 1 almost everywhere, and it is everywhere strictly less than 1 for positive a. For the lower bound, the two shifted U values sum to one and have product k; the paired p,q satisfy p^2+q^2=(2k+s)/(k+s+s^2), pq=sqrt(k/(k+s+s^2)). The deficits for p^2+q^2>=4/3 and pq>=2/3 reduce respectively to 2k-s-4s^2 and 5k-4s(1+s). Substitution of d=1-2a and v=cos(2phi) gives the printed two factorizations: both bracket factors are at least 1-d^2>0 for 0<a<1/2, making the inequalities strict unless d=0. Averaging the pair gives the exact lower endpoint, with a=0 handled separately. Thus the extrema are exactly the double-eigenvalue and zero-eigenvalue classes, respectively. This is analytic; the frozen eight-point numerical output is consistency evidence only.

value.rationale: This resolves the zonal-minimum candidate and identifies all minimizers in the first degree where the length is nonconstant across real harmonics. It is a geometric invariant of a canonical eigenspace, motivated by the previously posed sharp lower-bound question. The proof yields a useful spectrum-to-length formula and establishes strict optimality without needing a monotonicity assumption. It neither solves the higher-degree problem nor needs to in order to settle this nontrivial case.
